narrative.overview:
franC looks like the 1993 Saint-Exupéry 50 franc banknote held up under a lamp at night: deep night blue, a periwinkle engraving colour, a sand-coloured value, faint guilloché rosettes and a few stars. The name already says *franc* and *français*; the look says it again, quietly. It is a household tool, not a bank and not an AI product, so it avoids the cool grey "fintech" look, gradients on numbers, and glow.

It is an **Operate** surface used on a phone, one hand, a few seconds at a time. The banknote world lives in a few precise places (the hero value panel, the engraved section titles, the francs line, the page's faint rosettes). Everything else is calm, solid, dark cards with clear numbers in Manrope. One answer leads each screen; on Home it is Reste à vivre, set in an engraved serif like a note's face value.

**Status (2026-10-08):** this is the target system for the whole app and the only theme it will have (dark only). It ships on Home (Slice 57, SPEC §72), Opérations and the À valider queue (Slice 58, SPEC §73) and the Budget page at `/budget` (Slice 59, SPEC §74) and the lists you manage (Categories, Budgets and Goals settings, Paiements récurrents; Slice 60, SPEC §75) through the `.theme-50f` class. The other pages still render the older Tricolore light/dark tokens in `:root` until a roll-out slice migrates them; Tricolore is legacy, not a rule. Variants in the other last-series note colours (100 F Cézanne, 200 F Eiffel, 500 F Curie) may come later as alternative palettes on the same structure.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only: night page `#04051a`, solid note-blue cards `#121638` one step lighter, so cards stand out from the patterned page.
One accent, periwinkle `#8ea2ff`, for links, the active tab, section titles, charts and gauges.
Sand `#f3e3a6` is reserved for the hero amount, goal gauges and regular payments in budget gauges (paid solid, due hatched).
Amber `#ffb05a` is the only alarm colour. Red is never used, on amounts or anywhere else.
Three fonts with fixed jobs: Manrope for all text and numbers, Cormorant Garamond for the hero amount only, Cinzel capitals for titles.
Ten-block gauges instead of smooth progress bars.
Each section is its own titled card. No horizontal scroll at any width.

rules.name: The No Red Rule
rules.body: Red never appears inside the 50 F system. Money that needs attention is amber; nothing is ever "an error" in red. `--destructive` is amber.

rules.name: The Sand Is Money Rule
rules.body: Sand marks money you have or have already set aside: the hero amount, savings goals and regular payments. Nothing else takes it.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Periwinkle is the only accent. A new state gets a meaning from amber or mint, not a new hue. Category colours appear only as category markers (tinted icon tiles at 18 % alpha), never as UI chrome.

rules.name: The One Serif Number Rule
rules.body: Cormorant Garamond sets exactly one number per screen: the hero amount. Every other number is Manrope with tabular figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is the body default).

rules.name: The Francs Whisper Rule
rules.body: The amount in old francs (× 6,55957, legal rate, no inflation adjustment) appears in the Home Reste à vivre card only, nowhere else, and sits under the euro figure, right-aligned with it, 12px Faded Ink, and never extends past the euro amount's right edge. It is a wink; it never competes.

rules.name: The Pattern Below, Solid Above Rule
rules.body: Guilloché rosettes and stars live on the page background (`.bg-50f`) and inside the hero value panel only. Ordinary cards are solid Note Blue so their content reads cleanly.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: No glow, no gradient on numbers, no neon. The only gradient fills are the background pattern and the pace chart's area under the line.

dos: **Do** keep the 50 F system dark only; new screens add the `theme-50f` class (and `bg-50f` on the page wrapper) until the roll-out makes it the `:root` default.
**Do** lead every screen with one answer, and give each section its own Cinzel-titled card.
**Do** use Amber `#ffb05a` for every warning, over-budget and negative amount.
**Do** set every number in Manrope with tabular figures, except the one hero amount.
**Do** show the old price and the new price for a price rise, not "+2,50 €".
**Do** keep touch targets at least 44px and mark the active state with shape as well as colour.
**Do** format money and dates only through `lib/money.ts` and `lib/format-date.ts`.
Do make one tap do one job: choosing a category validates, and ✓ shows only when a row can be validated.
Do flag a transaction waiting for review with a small amber dot, never a coloured row.
Do write French month names in lower case inside a sentence (`inSentence`); the month title and sentence starts keep the capital.
**Do** keep a list and its summary on the same row component (`BudgetGaugeRowContent`, `GoalGaugeRowContent`) so the two never drift apart.
Do end a one-decision flow with the sticky action bar and one quiet text button below it; show the money a file will add (in, out, net) before the Import button.
Do keep a mint (`text-positive`) figure to gains and progress only; failure and warnings stay Amber.
donts: **Don't** use red anywhere, including for errors and destructive actions.
**Don't** add light-theme values or a theme picker to 50 F screens; Tricolore is legacy, not a reference (no page uses it any more since Slice 63).
**Don't** put gradients, glow or neon on numbers; no "banking/AI" sheen.
**Don't** use Bodoni Moda (its € reads as a C) or any second serif for numbers.
**Don't** put the rosette pattern on ordinary cards, or let decoration compete with a figure.
**Don't** allow horizontal scroll at any width.
**Don't** show actions on Home; it links to the pages where actions happen.
Don't show the francs line outside the Home card, or set any amount in a serif other than the Home hero.
Don't give a portal (sheet, toast, bulk bar) a hand-picked colour: add theme-50f to it.
**Don't** put a page's main "add" in the header on a list page: use the sticky bottom button.
**Don't** show "0 €" for an empty month on a category, or fold dormant categories away.
Don't hide a destructive step (Undo, Disconnect) as a loud button: it sits in a ⋯ menu or a quiet text button and confirms in a dialog.
